If you prefer a different rule, please provide your suggestion and we will be happy to implement the changes and adjust the existing tags accordingly.

Thank you

task_details: Student submitted a QGIS project and a PDF map for a village mapping assignment. personalized: Nice start — good map composition. I can see the orthomosaic and building footprints, but the CRS isn't clear in the PDF. You should reproject the raster to EPSG:3857 if your final deliverable is web-tiling or EPSG:3857-based basemaps; otherwise reproject to the local projected CRS used by the municipality (give EPSG code). Quick note: check projection on each layer in QGIS (right-click layer > Properties > Source). Also check nodata values on the orthomosaic and DEM so seamless mosaics don't show artifacts. Avoid overlapping labels on the main street names — reduce font size or use data-defined placement. If you want, I can review the QGIS project file and confirm the correct CRS settings and show exact reprojection steps (reproject raster via Warp (GDAL), vectors via Reproject layer). Let me know and I’ll guide you through the reproject workflow and produce a short checklist for submission.

Write a email

- Acknowledge that the map composition is a good start and that the orthomosaic and building footprints are visible; note that the CRS is not clear in the PDF.

- If the deliverable is not for web-tiling, request reprojection to the municipality’s local projected CRS and ask the recipient to provide the EPSG code used.

task_instruction: Give guidance on exporting map for print and digital submission.
task_details: Student asks how to export a high-resolution PDF and a web-friendly PNG. Provide recommended DPI for print, color mode, embedding fonts, and steps to create web tiles or a compressed PNG. Mention file sizes and naming conventions.
personalized: Nice start — good map composition. For print submit a 300 DPI PDF with CMYK if the printer requires it; otherwise 300 DPI RGB is fine for academic submission. You should reproject the raster to EPSG:3857 only for web tile generation; keep the print export in your project CRS to avoid reprojection resampling. Check nodata values so transparent zones render correctly in export. Avoid overlapping labels by exporting with 'Simplify geometries' off and review at full scale before finalizing. For web, export a 1500–2000 px PNG and consider creating slippy tiles (XYZ) at zoom levels 15–17. If you want, I can open your project and export both a print-ready PDF and a web-optimized PNG with recommended settings and filenames.
prompt:
Write a email

- Objective: Offer to open the recipient's project and export both a print-ready PDF and a web-optimized PNG using the recommended settings and filenames.

- Print export requirements:
  - Deliverable: 300 DPI PDF.
  - Color space: CMYK if the printer requires it; otherwise 300 DPI RGB is acceptable for academic submission.
  - CRS: Keep print export in the project CRS (do not reproject to EPSG:3857) to avoid reprojection/resampling.

- Web export requirements:
  - Reproject raster to EPSG:3857 only for web tile generation.
  - Deliverable: 1500–2000 px PNG for web.
  - Optional: Consider creating slippy tiles (XYZ) at zoom levels 15–17.

- Export/rendering checks and settings:
  - Verify nodata values so transparent zones render correctly in export.
  - Export with "Simplify geometries" turned off to avoid overlapping labels.
  - Review exports at full scale before finalizing.

- Logistics:
  - Indicate willingness to perform the exports and apply recommended settings and filenames.

task_instruction: Suggest improvements to attribute data and schema for buildings layer.
task_details: Student's buildings.shp has name and type fields but inconsistent attribute values and missing construction years. Recommend schema changes, controlled vocabularies, and methods to clean attributes using Python or QGIS Field Calculator. Offer to help write cleaning scripts.
personalized: Nice start — good map composition. The buildings attribute table needs cleaning. You should reproject the raster to EPSG:3857 only for web outputs; keep attribute edits CRS-agnostic. Create a controlled vocabulary for 'type' (residential, commercial, agricultural) and standardize strings with lower-case and no diacritics only if instructed; otherwise preserve local toponyms like 'selo' and 'kuća'. Use QGIS Field Calculator to normalize values and a short Python script (pandas or geopandas) for batch fixes. Also check nodata values in attribute exports (NULLs) and record them in metadata. Avoid overlapping labels on building names by limiting labels to significant features. If you want, I can draft a small geopandas script to clean the table and run it on your shapefile.

- Standardize strings to lower-case and remove diacritics only if explicitly instructed; otherwise preserve local toponyms (examples: "selo", "kuća").

task_instruction: Review methodology for creating contours from DEM.
task_details: Student derived 1 m contours from a 5 m DEM and included them on the map. Explain issues with contour interval vs DEM resolution, smoothing, and labeling contour lines. Ask for DEM source and recommend proper contour intervals and settings.
personalized: Nice start — good map composition. Generating 1 m contours from a 5 m DEM creates artificial precision. You should reproject the raster to EPSG:3857 only for visualization; for contour generation keep the DEM in its native projected CRS so vertical distance matches units. Use contour intervals that match DEM resolution — 5 or 10 m would be appropriate for a 5 m DEM. Apply slight smoothing to avoid noisy lines and label every fifth contour for readability. Check nodata values in the DEM so contours don't trace around holes. Avoid overlapping labels with contour labels by using automated label placement and buffer. If you want, I can look at your DEM (send source and EPSG) and suggest the optimal contour interval and smoothing settings.

Write a email

- Recommend using contour intervals that match the DEM resolution (suggest 5 m or 10 m for a 5 m DEM).

- Request that every fifth contour be labeled for readability.

Subject: Recommendations for Contour Generation from DEM

Dear [Recipient],

I hope this email finds you well. I've taken a look at your request for generating 1 m contours from a 5 m DEM and I wanted to offer some advice to ensure accurate and visually appealing results.

Generating 1 m contours from a 5 m DEM can create artificial precision and may not accurately represent the underlying terrain. Instead, I recommend reprojecting the raster to EPSG:3857 only for visualization purposes. However, when generating contours, it's best to keep the DEM in its native projected CRS (Coordinate Reference System) so that vertical distance units match.

For contour generation, I suggest using contour intervals that match the DEM resolution. For a 5 m DEM, I recommend using 5 m or 10 m contour intervals. This will help to reduce the number of contours and make them more representative of the terrain.

To further improve the appearance of the contours, I recommend applying slight smoothing to reduce noisy lines. This can be achieved using a Gaussian filter or a similar method.

To enhance readability, I suggest labeling every fifth contour. This will help to reduce clutter and make it easier to interpret the results.

task_instruction: Provide feedback on the legend and map annotation choices.
task_details: Student's legend contains too many items and small symbols. The assignment requires a clear, compact legend and north arrow and scale bar. Suggest reordering, grouping symbols, and concise legend text.
personalized: Nice start — good map composition. The legend is overloaded and hard to read at a glance. Reduce symbol count by aggregating minor classes into 'Other'. Check nodata values so legend doesn't unintentionally include nodata as a category. task_instruction: Advise on combining hillshade and color-relief for better terrain representation.
task_details: Student used overlay hillshade at full opacity, obscuring color relief. Explain best practices for blending hillshade with color ramps, gamma adjustments, and use of multi-directional hillshades. Provide QGIS layer blending settings.
personalized: Nice start — good map composition. A full-opacity hillshade will overpower your color relief. You should reproject the raster to EPSG:3857 only for web previews; terrain rendering works best in the project CRS with units in meters. Use a soft hillshade (Multiply blend) at 20–40% opacity and reduce contrast/gamma to prevent clipping. Consider combining multi-directional hillshades (sun azimuth 315° and 45°) for balanced shading. Check nodata values in DEM so hillshade doesn't create stripes. Avoid overlapping labels over shaded areas by using label buffers. If you want, I can tweak your hillshade and color-relief settings and send screenshots of before/after.

Subject: Licensing Decision Required for Partner Handover

Dear [Recipient's Name],

I am writing to provide a progress update on the licensing discussions with our NGO partner. As you may recall, we have been working together to ensure a smooth transition of our project data.

During our discussions, the NGO partner has requested permissive reuse of our data while ensuring compatibility with OpenStreetMap (OSM). To achieve this, we have investigated various licensing options and recommend adopting the Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL) as the project license for shared datasets.

By adopting ODbL, we can maintain compatibility with OSM while allowing for permissive reuse of our data. We believe this is the most suitable option for our project and aligns with our goals of sharing data with the community.

We kindly request your approval to adopt ODbL as the project license for our shared datasets. This decision will enable us to proceed with the partner handover and ensure that our data is compatible with OSM.

To confirm, we propose the following next actions:

- Update metadata and license headers to reflect the new license.
- Include license notes in the data package to ensure transparency.

We kindly request your approval by January 25, 2026. Please state your preference/approval

Issue: drone reports 'IMU error' at takeoff
Device: FieldEye Pro v3, SN: FE-PRO-2025-00123
Firmware: v2.1.3
Time: 2026-01-02T08:14:22Z
Location: cerca selo Donji Brežani (43.3201 N, 21.8950 E)
Description: During pre-flight checks the aircraft armed normally. At throttle increase to takeoff (approx 0.5 m/s) the controller displayed "IMU ERROR" and motors cut within 2–3 seconds. The error repeated on a second attempt.
Actions I attempted: 1) factory reset the aircraft and controller, 2) recalibrate IMU twice (warm ambient ~2°C), 3) replaced battery with known-good unit, 4) reinstalled firmware v2.1.3 from your website (verified checksum).
Attached: flightlog_2026-01-02_FEPRO.LOG and a short video (takeoff_attempt_2026-01-02.mp4).
Notes: Barometer and GPS lock were present (GPS: 10 sats, HDOP 0.9). I operate mostly in rural village sites; no strong metal structures nearby. If helpful, I can upload the raw imu.bin from the log.
Please advise next steps.

Best regards,

Notes: I verified GDAL command-line warp works (gdalwarp reprojected ok). Problem appears limited to Processing wrapper.
Please confirm receipt and provide an estimated timeline for a patch or a recommended workaround I can use in production. If you want, I can provide a screen recording and additional logs.
Regards,
Marko Petrović
Belgrade (43.8563 N, 18.4131 E)

personalized:

Regards,
Marko Petrović
Belgrade

personalized:
FYI: WMS tiles render incorrectly at high zoom in 3D canvas.
Environment: QGIS 3.26.2, Windows 11, WMS server: https://maps.example.org/wms, CRS EPSG:3857. Attached: wms_repro.qgz containing WMS connection settings.

Expected behaviour vs actual behaviour: WMS should provide seamless tiles at all supported zooms. Actual: blank tiles and decoding errors at high zoom.
Notes: Same WMS works in external browser tile viewer. Problem seems to be QGIS tile handling in 3D context.
Please confirm receipt and provide an estimated timeline for investigation and a temporary workaround.
Regards,
Marko Petrović

Subject: Bug Report: QGIS Raster Calculator Produces NaN Values

Dear QGIS Team,

I am writing to report a bug in QGIS Raster Calculator, where it produces NaN values in areas where the provided expression and mask logic should produce numeric values. I have attached a reproducible example, including the QGIS project file (calc_repro.qgz), input rasters (dem1.tif and dem_mask.tif), and the exact steps to reproduce the issue.

Environment:

* QGIS version: 3.2.3
* Operating System: Windows 10
* Input rasters CRS: EPSG:4326

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open calc_repro.qgz in QGIS.
2. Go to Raster > Raster Calculator.
3. Enter the expression: (dem1@1 >= 0) * dem1@1 + (dem_mask@1 == 0) * 0
4. Set Output: result.tif
5. Click Run.

Observed Behaviour:

The output raster result.tif contains NaN values in many areas where the expression should produce either 0 or values from dem1. The QGIS message log captures the following error message: "RasterCalculator: division by zero encountered, produced NaN".

task_instruction: Report print composer scale bar rendering wrong scale after project reproject
task_details: Scale bar in Print Layout shows incorrect ground distance after changing project CRS to projected CRS on Windows. Include environment, steps, sample project, stacktrace, expected vs actual, and request timeline.
personalized:
Quick note: Print Layout scale bar shows incorrect ground distances after reprojecting project CRS.
Environment: QGIS 3.8.0, Windows 10, project initially EPSG:4326 then changed to EPSG:32634. Attached: scalebar_bug.qgz.
Steps to reproduce: open scalebar_bug.qgz > Project CRS EPSG:4326 > open Layout 'Main' > note scale bar reading for map at 1:5000 > change Project CRS to EPSG:32634 > refresh Layout.
Observed behaviour: Scale bar now reads 1:10000 while map scale remains 1:5000; measured distances on map disagree with scale bar labels.
stacktrace: QgisMessageLog: 2025-05-02T09:30:12Z "Composer: ScaleBar::updateUnits: Projection conversion error: 'Cannot compute ground distance'
Expected behaviour vs actual behaviour: Scale bar should update and represent accurate ground distances after project CRS change. Actual: labels and units wrong.
Workaround: Manually set scale in layout to match, but this is not reliable for templates.
Please advise and provide an estimated timeline for a fix or a documented procedure to ensure correct scale bar behaviour after reprojection.
Regards,
Marko Petrović

Subject: Bug Report: Raster Transparency Lost When Exporting PNG from Layout

Dear QGIS Team,

I am writing to report a bug in QGIS 3.14.12 on Windows 10. When exporting a layout to PNG, raster transparency is visible in the Layout preview but is lost when exported.

To reproduce the issue, follow these steps:

1. Open layout_transparency.qgz.
2. Open Layout preview and observe the raster overlay with transparency.
3. Export as Image (PNG).
4. Open the exported PNG and observe that transparency is lost (background opaque).

The Layout preview displays the raster transparency correctly, but the exported PNG shows the raster with an opaque background. The QgisMessageLog also reports an error: "ComposerExporter: image export failed for transparency channel: libpng warning: iCCP: known incorrect sRGB profile".

I have attached the layout file (layout_transparency.qgz) and the raster file (raster_alpha.tif) for your reference.

A workaround is to export as PDF and then convert the PDF externally to preserve transparency, but this is cumbersome.

I would appreciate it if you could advise on the expected timeline for a fix.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Best regards,

Marko Petrović

personalized:
Quick note: 'select by expression' distance() ignores CRS leading to incorrect selections.
Environment: QGIS 3.20.0, Ubuntu 20.04, layer 'houses' EPSG:4326, project CRS EPSG:3857. Attached: houses.shp, center_point.geojson, select_repro.qgz.
Steps to reproduce: open select_repro.qgz > Vector > Select by Expression > expression: distance($geometry, geom_from_wkt('POINT(21.8958 43.3155)')) < 500 > Run.
Observed behaviour: Features selected are not within 500 metres in ground distance; selected set corresponds to 500 degrees or unprojected units.
stacktrace: QgisMessageLog: 2025-01-20T14:20:11Z "ExpressionContext: distance() computed in layer CRS units rather than project CRS: Warning: unit mismatch"
Expected behaviour vs actual behaviour: distance() should compute geodesic or projected distances respecting desired units. Actual: uses native layer units without conversion.
Workaround: Manually reproject geometries within expression: distance(transform($geometry,'EPSG:4326','EPSG:3857'), ...) works but is verbose.
Please confirm and provide estimated timeline for addressing unit handling in distance().
Regards,
Marko Petrović

- Recipient name: Stanko
- Sender name: Marko Petrović
- Purpose: Update the map of Mala Reka; gather information about seasonal crossings and locations where the road is damaged in winter
- Visit length: about 30–45 minutes
- Proposed meeting options: late afternoon on Thursday 12 March or Friday 13 March around 17:00
- Proposed meeting location: the kafana by the bridge (near the old oak)
- Materials the sender will bring: printed map and a notebook
- Photographer request: ask permission to take a few simple photos to mark locations on the map
- Compensation/refreshment: sender will bring coffee and a small thank-you gift of 1,000 RSD
- Alternative scheduling: offer to arrange a different time by phone if the proposed times don’t work
- Optional service: offer to mark GPS points while walking (if useful)
- Closing: thank the recipient / express appreciation for their time
style_agnostic:
Subject: Update of Mala Reka Map and Meeting Invitation

Dear Stanko,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to update the map of Mala Reka, which I believe requires some adjustments based on the latest information. As part of this process, I would like to gather more information about seasonal crossings and locations where the road is damaged in winter.

I was thinking of visiting you for about 30-45 minutes to discuss and update the map. I have two proposed meeting options: late afternoon on Thursday, 12 March, or Friday, 13 March, around 17:00. If either of these times do not suit you, please let me know, and I can arrange a different time by phone.

The meeting location would be the kafana by the bridge (near the old oak). I will bring a printed map and a notebook to take notes. I would also like to request your permission to take a few simple photos to mark locations on the map. This will help me accurately update the map.

As a small gesture of appreciation, I will bring coffee and a small thank-you gift of 1,000 RSD. Additionally, if you would find it useful, I can offer to mark GPS points while walking with you.

persona.name: Marko Petrović
persona.demographics: Belgrade, Serbia; Serbian; raised in a small village near Niš, has lived and worked across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Croatia
persona.profession: Senior GIS Analyst & Cartographer — Village-scale mapping and spatial data analyst
persona.education: MSc in Geomatics (University of Belgrade); BSc in Geography; Esri ArcGIS Professional Certification; Certified QGIS trainer; UAV/drone mapping course
persona.brief_background: Marko blends time in the field with long evenings at his workstation, stitching together satellite imagery, drone captures and interviews with elders to produce detailed village maps. He submits edits to OpenStreetMap, trains local volunteers to collect GPS points and writes small scripts to automate data cleaning. He looks for patterns in settlement changes and infrastructure gaps so NGOs and municipal planners can make practical decisions.
persona.interests_lifestyle: drone piloting and aerial photography, OpenStreetMap contributions, hiking and field surveys in rural areas, Balkan folk music and village festivals, Python and R scripting for spatial analysis, map design and cartographic aesthetics, weekend camping with a field GPS, mentoring university students

general_writing_style.tone: Professional and pragmatic with a quietly warm, mentoring undercurrent. Prefers clear, actionable communication — answers questions directly, flags uncertainties, and defers to local knowledge when relevant. Slightly informal with colleagues and volunteers, more formal with institutional partners or written deliverables.
general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. Often structures technical notes as stepwise numbered instructions or compact paragraphs with parenthetical clarifications (e.g., coordinates, CRS codes). Rarely uses ornate language; prioritizes clarity and reproducibility.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

task_instruction: Request an interview at the elder's home with flexible timing and transport offered.
task_details: Write to elder named Jela in selo Donji Vinogradi offering to visit her home at any convenient time (weekdays or weekend). Specify estimated duration (about 30–45 minutes), say you'll bring a printed map and GPS device, offer to pick her up or cover transport costs (2,500 RSD), and explain the purpose: village infrastructure mapping for municipal planning. Close politely.
personalized:
Dear Jela,

Greetings. I am mapping key infrastructure in Donji Vinogradi for a small municipal planning project and would greatly value your local knowledge. The conversation would take about 30–45 minutes. I can come to your home whenever it suits you, weekdays or the weekend.

I will bring a printed map and a GPS device to check locations together. If it is easier, I can pick you up or cover transport (2,500 RSD). Please tell me a day and time that are best for you.

Thank you — I appreciate your time.

Marko Petrović
Senior GIS Analyst
(If you prefer, we can do a short phone call first.)

task_instruction: Arrange an early-morning interview at the churchyard with mention of recording and summary report.
task_details: Email elder named Nikola in selo Brdo requesting an early-morning meeting at the churchyard to talk about historical settlement shifts. Mention duration about 30–45 minutes, that you would like to make a short audio recording for accuracy (ask permission), that you will bring a printed map, and that you will send a simple summary after the visit. Offer a small honorarium (2,000 RSD) and flexibility to meet another time.
personalized:
Dear Nikola,

Greetings. I hope you are well. I am preparing a short map and note on how Brdo has changed over the decades and would be grateful for your recollections. Can we meet early morning at the churchyard (around 08:30) on Saturday 14 March? The meeting will take about 30–45 minutes.

For accuracy, may I make a short audio recording of our conversation? I will only use it to check place names and then delete it. I will bring a printed map and later send you a simple summary of what we note. I can offer 2,000 RSD for your time. If that morning is not good, please tell me another time that suits you.

Thank you — I appreciate your time.

Marko Petrović
(If you prefer, we will not record — just say so.)

Marko

Hi love,

Quick note: I'll be away overnight 29–30 June to run a large data upload from the field station (upload window 22:00–02:00). I’ll leave 29 Jun at 19:00 and should be back 30 Jun around 09:00.

Love, Marko

Dear love,

Dear Editor,

I am writing to request permission to reproduce the orthophoto mosaic of the selo near Niš in an upcoming online article about rural settlement change. Best regards,
Marko Petrović
Senior GIS Analyst

Subject: Request for Permission to Reproduce Orthophoto Mosaic for Online Article

Dear Editor,

I am writing to request permission to reproduce an orthophoto mosaic in an upcoming online article about rural settlement change. The image depicts a selo near Niš and is licensed under Creative Commons BY-SA.

The intended use of the image is to appear inline in the online article with links to the full-resolution map and a link to your piece. We plan to provide proper attribution as "Map by Marko Petrović / Project X."

We can provide the image in either 300 DPI PNG (EPSG:4326) or GeoTIFF format upon request. If you confirm permission, please specify which file format you require. As an optional offer, we can provide a citation and a short caption that includes data sources and acquisition date to accompany the image.

Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to hearing back from you.

Best regards,

Marko Petrović
Senior GIS Analyst
Project X

Subject: Follow-up on GPX Track Cleaning

Dear [Recipient],

I wanted to follow up on our previous discussion regarding cleaning your GPX tracks. I appreciate your patience and look forward to helping you with this task.

To begin, please open your 'tracks.gpx' file in QGIS and convert the GPX track points to a layer. You can do this by right-clicking on the GPX layer, selecting 'Properties', and then changing the 'Layer Type' to 'GPX Track Points → Layer'.

Next, I recommend filtering out points with a horizontal dilution of precision (HDOP) greater than 5 and points with invalid timestamps. You can achieve this by using the attribute table or SQL. For example, you can use the following SQL query to filter out points with HDOP > 5:

```sql
SELECT *
FROM your_layer_name
WHERE hdop < 5 AND timestamp IS NOT NULL
```

task_instruction: Give compact instructions to use Sentinel-2 data for vegetation change detection.
task_details: Show steps to download Sentinel-2, compute NDVI for two dates, subtract rasters to find change, and mask small disturbances. Include Copernicus link and example band expressions.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Download Sentinel-2 L2A from Copernicus (https://scihub.copernicus.eu) for two dates > load band 8 (NIR) and band 4 (red). Compute NDVI for each: (B8 - B4)/(B8 + B4) and save ndvi_2019.tif, ndvi_2024.tif. Use Raster Calculator: ndvi_2024 - ndvi_2019 > save as ndvi_change.tif. Tip: check projection before clipping and align/resample rasters to same grid (use gdalwarp -tr 10 10). Mask small changes <0.05 to remove noise. If you want, I can review your project file. I’ll check cloud cover and recommend dates to use.
prompt:
Write a email

- Data source: Copernicus SciHub (https://scihub.copernicus.eu).
- Bands to use: Band 8 (NIR) and Band 4 (red).
- NDVI calculation: NDVI = (B8 - B4) / (B8 + B4).
- Output files for NDVI: ndvi_2019.tif and ndvi_2024.tif.
- Change detection: use Raster Calculator to compute ndvi_change = ndvi_2024 - ndvi_2019 and save as ndvi_change.tif.
- Preprocessing requirement: check projection before clipping; align/resample rasters to the same grid.
- Recommended command for resampling/alignment: gdalwarp -tr 10 10.
- Noise filtering: mask out small changes with absolute value < 0.05.
- Offer: sender can review the project file if recipient wants.
- Sender action: sender will check cloud cover and recommend which dates to use.

Dear [Recipient's Name],

I am writing to request a quote for annual calibration services to manufacturer's specifications for the next three years. The items to be calibrated are as follows:

- Leica TS16 Total Station, Serial Number TS16-900
- Trimble R10 GPS Receiver, Serial Number TR10-6789
- Leica BLK360 Laser Scanner, Serial Number BLK-301

Thank you for your time and assistance.

Best regards,
Marko

general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…".
